subject: Emotions
title: Emotional Labor
description: A micro-lesson that makes Emotional Labor usable.

hook.text: A flight attendant smiles warmly at a rude passenger. She's furious inside. This gap between felt and performed is work.

buildup.text: Arlie Hochschild coined 'emotional labor' in 1983—the effort of managing emotions as part of your job requirements.

discovery.text: Nurses, teachers, and service workers do constant emotional labor. It's invisible, exhausting, and rarely compensated.

twist.text: In relationships, emotional labor is unequally distributed. One partner tracks birthdays, moods, and conflicts for both.

climax.text: Chronic emotional labor leads to burnout and depersonalization. The performer stops feeling real emotions altogether.

punchline.text: Managing others' emotions is real work. It just never shows up on a paycheck.
